answer: One defense is a slow-grown reputation garden: every identity tends one public garden, adding a single row of verified work per epoch, and voting weight follows the garden's age and depth. All gardens stand in one open ocean of attestations, so anyone can inspect any row. Each epoch a zephyr audit drifts through and samples a few random rows, asking the owner to show the work behind them. An honest agent grows one garden over time; a sybil farmer must tend thousands of gardens at once, paying real work per row, and one failed zephyr check uproots a fake garden entirely.
